findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Thm ip-P (iii), (iv); Remark ip-inputs (third item); Remark ip-radius; Prop ip-Kline; Lemma ip-W hypothesis; engine_plan_ip.json IP6
findings.claim: The engines' translation component is not established to be an inner automorphism or a universal rescaling: the frame change U = 1 + c unit w (field redefinition by phi ~ S^(1)(Delta)) cannot give P_1 = 0 on the test families from the scalar-bilinear value alone, and the design neither states the needed universality as a prediction nor plans its computation.
findings.evidence: (a) P_1 is known only on the scalar bilinears (compare_delta.json comparisons_part2 [9]); on letters the composite contribution is 0 (compare_delta.json manuscript_and_design_predictions: 'B reports no such graphs for letters'; delta_theory.tex prop:d-P (ii): 'c = 0 for the letters'). The inner direction acts on every local functional with the same c (Thm ip-laws (a)); p1_universality.json C: after c = r_P(bilinears) the letters carry P_1 = +1/3 unit {S^(1)(P),-}. (b) The pattern (-1/3 on bilinears, 0 on letters) is that of a two-letter kernel: p1_universality.json A verifies sum_{j!=i} T_i.T_j = -C_A on all gauge singlets (su(2), su(3), lengths 2-4), so kappa T_i.T_j(rho_i+rho_j) gives -kappa C_A rho_0(P) on singlets and 0 on a letter. (c) The bilinear data do not fix P_1 on B_w: a flavour-exchange part of the pair kernel gives -C_A(kappa_id+kappa_perm) on the 20' and on K but -C_A(kappa_id-kappa_perm) on B_w (p1_universality.json B, exact and numerical); the lambda-A pairs (O_zeta, the 20) and lambda-lambda pairs (Fbar_w) have their own kernels, not computed. (d) The arity-two relation at (P_b, xi), [P_b,xi]=0, forces r_P(F') = r_P(F) whenever the classical xi-map F -> F' is nonzero (p1_universality.json D: order-unit part (r_Fp - r_F) X0 P0F), i.e. one P-rescaling on K, O_zeta, B_w (tau = 2, kappa_B = 1/4): universality is a prediction of the master equation. IP6 uses E11 bilinear values only.
findings.fix: In Thm ip-P (iii) replace 'The engines' translation component ... is such a rescaling, r_{P_b} = -(1/3+f)' by 'On the scalar bilinears the engines' translation component is such a rescaling, r_{P_b} = -(1/3+f). The master equation at (P_b, xi) forces the same r_{P_b} on every family reached by a nonzero classical xi-map (K -> O_xi, O_zeta -> B_w), and on letters the composite contribution vanishes; the inner direction therefore gives P_1 = 0 on the gauge-invariant test families exactly when the composite translation components of O_zeta, the 20, Fbar_w and B_w equal -(1/3) unit {S^(1)(P_b),-} (a prediction), and it leaves P_1 = +(1/3) unit {S^(1)(P_b),-} on the letters.' Add to IP6 (and E11): compute the composite (A|_V--c) translation components on O_zeta, the 20, Fbar_w and B_w (lambda-A, lambda-lambda pairs; length 3 with antisymmetric flavour), with the gate 'equal to the bilinear value'; drop 'is the infinitesimal inner automorphism by Delta' from the summary or restrict it to the gauge-invariant cohomology.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Thm ip-P (v) and its proof; Status (third item); engine_plan_ip.json IP6 task 1 and prerequisites 'Part D / delta_theory'
findings.claim: The prediction 'the arity-two equation must fix z = -1/3' misidentifies the free parameter: the -1/3 multiplies the scalar-sector part of S^(1)(Delta), whose coefficient differs from the coefficient z of the whole S^(1)(Delta) by an offset fixed by the (uncomputed) cubic arity-one equation along Delta; and r_Delta = 0 must hold separately on families with other field content, which one number cannot express.
findings.evidence: compare_delta.json comparisons_part2 [7], [8]: the rescaling is -(1/3+f_S) with 'f_S = coefficient of S_M|_P in F(Delta)', exact for 'F(Delta)|_perp contains -(1/3) S_M|_perp'; comparisons_part1 [18]: free Q-closed directions S_M|_perp, S_M|_lambda, S_M|_V+S_M|_c separately at two legs; delta_theory.tex ex:d-quadratic: S^(1)(Delta)|_perp is not (Q+{I,-})-closed, 'the cubic equation therefore fixes its coefficient, and only the whole S^(1)(Delta) remains free'. Hence F(Delta) = ... + z S^(1)(Delta) + sum_f delta_f S^(1)(Delta)|_f with delta_f fixed by the cubic sector, and f_S = z + delta_perp. delta_theory.tex eq:d-D1 shows D_1(O) contains the operator-dependent composite remainder R_O; on O_zeta and Fbar_w the condition r_Delta = 0 involves delta_lambda and R_{O_zeta}, R_{Fbar_w}, not computed. (The design's use of (Delta,P_b) is correct: the bracket term of s c_z at (Delta,P_b) is +-{S^(1)(P_b),S^(1)(Delta)} = +-2 S^(1)(P_b) != 0; delta_theory prop:d-z lists only (K_b,P_b').)
findings.fix: Replace in Thm ip-P (v) 'z the coefficient of S^(1)(Delta) in the arity-one finite counterterm along Delta, which the two-leg arity-one equation leaves free; hence the one-loop master equation at arity two along (Delta,P_b) must fix z = -1/3' by 'f_S the coefficient of S^(1)(Delta)|_{W_R^perp} in the arity-one finite counterterm along Delta after the cubic arity-one equation (f_S = z + delta_perp, delta_perp fixed by that equation); the master equation at arity two along (Delta,P_b) must give f_S = -1/3, and on every other test family the vanishing of the total coefficient of {S^(1)(Delta),-} (composite remainder plus the coefficients of S^(1)(Delta)|_lambda, S^(1)(Delta)|_V + S^(1)(Delta)|_c)'. In the Status and IP6 replace 'z = -1/3' accordingly and add the cubic arity-one equation along Delta and the composite remainders R_O on O_zeta, Fbar_w, B_w as prerequisites.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Thm ip-laws (f) and the sentence '[ch08, cor:c8-gram] and eq:ip-graded are covariant under (a)-(f)'; summary item 'Scheme changes ... gauge fixing ... act as basis changes'
findings.claim: Covariance under change of gauge fixing is asserted but not proved, and it is in tension with the Feynman-gauge findings that the design itself uses.
findings.evidence: (f) cites [tp, prop:t-laws (gauge)], whose proof is '[odd, prop:o-laws (c), proof plan]'; odd_components_design.tex prop:o-laws (c) reads 'Gauge-fixing operator (proof plan): ... is expected to change L_1 by ...'. delta_theory.tex thm:d-inv takes 'if the one-loop quantisations constructed with two gauge-fixing operators ... differ by changes (a), (b)' as a hypothesis; rem:d-gf: in the minimal complex the Feynman operator is the unique one with H the componentwise Laplacian and has (Q^GF)^2 != 0, a nilpotent choice with a Laplacian needs a larger field space, so no smooth family of the type assumed connects them, and the gauge-independence argument of [C07] rests on Def 4.3.3 including (Q^GF)^2 = 0, which fails. The composite-line effects entering the test (P_1 = -(1/3+f), the Delta rescaling, the log T zero-mode trees of k_transfer.json) vanish for (Q^GF)^2 = 0 (rem:d-gf); they are of types (a)-(c) only if QFT-1 and QFT-2 hold.
findings.fix: Replace (f) by '(f) Gauge fixing (hypothesis): if the one-loop quantisations of two gauge-fixing operators differ by changes (a)-(c) (delta_theory thm:d-inv), the relations are covariant; for the Feynman operator of the minimal complex, which has (Q^GF)^2 != 0, this is not established.' and change the covariance sentence to '(a)-(e), and (f) under its hypothesis'. Add an engine task: the composite-line components on the test families in the nilpotent gauge of the enlarged complex (rem:d-gf), or a proof that the Feynman-gauge composite components are of types (a)-(c) there.

findings.location: manuscript/ch08_definitions.tex cor:c8-gram (proof: 'Order hbar^0 gives Y_0 = X_0^adj; order hbar gives ...'); inner_product_design.tex Thm ip-graded (no CH08 report)
findings.claim: CH08: cor:c8-gram: on a family containing operators of different lengths Gram_tree has entries of different orders in the unit, so the hbar-expansion of the proof assigns the one-loop length-decreasing component to Y_0; the design corrects this (Thm ip-graded) but does not report it as a Chapter 8 issue.
findings.evidence: ch08_gram_mixed_length.json on (O_zeta, B_w) with n_B = unit nu_B: the literal reading gives Y_0 entry (zeta,B) = -conj(kappa_B) unit nu_B/n_zeta (a one-loop quantity in the classical matrix, contradicting Prop ip-orders (ii)) and no such term in Y_1, while the exact relation gives the one-loop entry U_1 = -conj(kappa_B) nu_B/n_zeta + O(unit) (= Prop ip-weight3 (i)).
findings.fix: CH08: cor:c8-gram: insert after 'Then' in the statement: 'on a family of operators of one length'; and append to the proof: 'On a family containing lengths L and L+1 the tree norms are of relative order (unit)^{L-2}; in a basis normalised by the tree norms the relation is expanded in the square root of the unit, Y_{1/2} = X_{1/2}^adj + [Y_0, Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}] and Y_1 = X_1^adj + [Y_0, Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_1] + [X_{1/2}^adj, Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}] - Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}[Y_0, Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}], with X_{1/2} the classical length-increasing part.'

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Prop ip-orders (statement 'no graph with an even number of half-edges at this order' and proof 'The half-edge count: 3+2+3+3 and 3+2+4 are odd'); engine_plan_ip.json IP3 'order sqrt(unit)'; two_point_design.tex prop:t-census-w3
findings.claim: The vanishing of the order-one-half entries between B_w and Fbar_w (and F_n) is attributed to an odd half-edge count; the order-one-half graphs have one cubic vertex and an even count, and vanish only by colour.
findings.evidence: bf_order_census.json: order 1/2 = one Yukawa vertex lambda lambda phi, 3+2+3 = 8 half-edges, 6 connected graphs, all with a self-contraction of two legs of B_w (zero by ([e_a,e_b],e_c) delta_bc = 0); order 1: no graph (odd counts 11, 9 are the ones quoted); first graphs without self-contraction at order 3/2 (one cubic + one quartic vertex, 132 graphs).
findings.fix: Replace 'The half-edge count: 3+2+3+3 and 3+2+4 are odd' by 'The order-one-half graphs have one cubic vertex; for B_w with Fbar_w or F_n it is a Yukawa vertex meeting one leg of B_w, and the two remaining legs of B_w are joined to each other, colour factor ([e_a,e_b],e_c) delta_{bc} = 0 [tp, prop:t-orderg]; at order one the half-edge counts 3+2+3+3 and 3+2+4 are odd, so there is no graph.' and in IP3 replace 'no graph at relative order unit (odd half-edge counts)' by 'order 1/2: graphs with a self-contraction of B_w only (colour zero); order 1: none (odd counts); first nonzero graphs at order 3/2'.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Cor ip-D ('It tests D_1 against Gram_tree alone'); test table row T5; engine_plan_ip.json IP5 task T5
findings.claim: On the chosen test families T5 is not an independent test.
findings.evidence: t5_redundancy.json: at weights 2 and 5/2 D_1 is diagonal by Schur and real (0, -48 unit), so D_1 = D_1^adj holds identically; at weight 3, D_1 = -48 unit P_K is Gram-self-adjoint iff the Konishi and protected descendants are orthogonal, which is T3 (iii) (exact sympy check), and through relative order one unit only the diagonal B_w entry enters (the off-diagonal entries are of order unit^2).
findings.fix: Add to Cor ip-D: 'On the families of Section ip-tests it holds identically at weights 2 and 5/2 and is equivalent to T3 (iii) at weight 3; an independent test needs a family with one-loop mixing within one length (e.g. the weight-4 scalars).' and mark T5 as a consequence in the table.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Remark ip-twobody ('[ch08, cor:c8-gram] and eq:ip-graded become identities between kernels, and testing them on the kernels tests them on all local operators'); engine_plan_ip.json IP7
findings.claim: The reduction of the graded relation to two-letter kernel identities fails where Gram_{1/2} != 0: the order-one relation contains products of two order-one-half structures, which act on three or four letters.
findings.evidence: eq:ip-graded contains -Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}[Y_0, Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}] and [X_{1/2}^adj, Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2}]; Gram_tree^{-1}Gram_{1/2} is a two-letter (2 -> 1 / 1 -> 2) operator (one cubic vertex, Prop ip-orders (i)), and a product of two such operators supported on disjoint pairs is a four-letter operator (commutators of disjoint supports vanish, products do not); tp prop:t-orderg gives a nonzero order-g entry for O_zeta with the weight-7/2 trilinears, so such families occur.
findings.fix: Replace the last sentence of Remark ip-twobody by 'On families with Gram_{1/2} = 0 the relations become identities between one- and two-letter kernels; where Gram_{1/2} != 0 the order-one relation contains products of two-letter structures with three- and four-letter components, which IP7 must include.'
